folio_number_inscription.description: The numeral '104' written in brown ink at the top-right corner of the parchment, functioning as a modern or semi-contemporary folio number. It sits above and slightly overlapping the first text line. Likely added by a later archivist. Small in size, approximately 40 normalized units wide and 30 tall.

paragraph_break_marker_P1.description: A tall decorated initial or paragraph-opening mark in the left margin at the very start of the folio's first paragraph (f104r.1). In the Stars section, paragraph openings are often marked by a slightly enlarged or flourished initial glyph. This mark is the leftmost visible glyph of line 1, sitting at the inner margin boundary. Height spans approximately one line height.

paragraph_break_marker_P2.description: Paragraph mark at the start of the second paragraph group, aligning with approximately the 10th text line from the top. Marks a thematic division within the Stars section content. Visible as a slightly enlarged or specially-formed initial glyph at the left margin.

paragraph_break_marker_P3.description: Paragraph mark at the start of the third paragraph group, at approximately line 20. Marks another thematic break. Sits flush against the left text margin, consistent with all other paragraph markers.

paragraph_break_marker_P4.description: Paragraph mark at the start of the fourth paragraph group, at approximately line 30. The large paragraph blocks that precede this marker show the most densely-packed text on the folio.

paragraph_break_marker_P5.description: Paragraph mark at the start of the fifth and final paragraph group at approximately line 36. The remaining paragraph (lines 36–45) constitutes the closing block of the folio and terminates before the bottom margin.

star_1_marginalia.description: An 8-pointed star drawn in dark brown/reddish ink in the left margin, positioned alongside the first paragraph group (lines 1–3). The star is rendered with alternating long and short points in a compass-rose pattern, filled or partially filled with red pigment. It sits entirely within the left margin gutter, to the left of the main text body, and does not interact with or bisect any text line. Stars in this folio section function as visual paragraph or entry separators.

star_2_marginalia.description: 8-pointed margin star, positioned alongside lines 4–6. Same compass-rose style with reddish-brown ink. Slightly larger than star_1. No text bisection — the text body begins fully to the right of all star drawings at x_min ~115.

star_3_marginalia.description: 8-pointed margin star alongside lines 7–9. Drawn with slightly more elongated points than the preceding stars, giving a more spindly silhouette. Red/brown ink, consistent with the section's visual vocabulary.

star_4_marginalia.description: A smaller 6-pointed (or possibly 8-pointed but more compact) star aligned with lines 11–13. Its smaller size may indicate a different sub-category or entry type within the Stars section taxonomy.

star_5_marginalia.description: 8-pointed red-outlined star alongside lines 14–16. This star appears to be drawn with a heavier outline stroke and possibly outline-only (not solid-filled), making it visually distinct from the filled stars above. Consistent left-margin positioning.

star_6_marginalia.description: 8-pointed margin star alongside lines 17–19. Returns to the standard filled style. Slightly tilted on its axis compared to the perfectly upright preceding stars, suggesting natural variation in hand-drawing across the folio.

star_7_marginalia.description: 8-pointed margin star alongside lines 20–22. Well-centered in the margin column. The paragraph break marker (P3) at approximately this y-level means this star may additionally mark the conceptual start of the third content block.

star_8_marginalia.description: 8-pointed margin star alongside lines 23–25. Standard style. Positioned at the vertical midpoint of the folio, approximately y=510–575.

star_9_marginalia.description: 8-pointed margin star alongside lines 27–29. Standard compass-rose style. Notably, the text line f104r.26 is a very short line ('shar.sheey.kar.sheody') suggesting a paragraph or stanza break at that point, making this star a likely separator marker.

star_10_marginalia.description: An outline-only (hollow) 8-pointed star alongside lines 30–32. This hollow rendering is distinctive and may indicate a different classification of entry, a star that was begun but not inked in fully, or a specific scribal notation. It is the most visually unusual of the margin stars on this folio.

star_11_marginalia.description: 8-pointed margin star alongside lines 33–35. Returns to filled style. Ink is slightly lighter/more faded compared to the dark-red stars earlier in the folio, possibly due to less pigment loaded on the pen at that point in the scribe's work session.

star_12_marginalia.description: A smaller, compact star alongside lines 36–38. Possibly 6-pointed. Marks the start of the fifth paragraph block. Consistent left-margin position but reduced size echoes star_4's role as a sub-entry marker.

star_13_marginalia.description: 8-pointed red star alongside lines 39–41. One of the more vividly pigmented stars on the page, with a strong reddish-brown fill. Standard compass-rose morphology.

star_14_marginalia.description: 8-pointed margin star alongside lines 42–45, the final paragraph block. Standard style. Its position near the page bottom means the lowest point of this star is approximately y=1000 — the very bottom margin of the parchment.

gutter_binding_edge.description: The physical left binding gutter of the manuscript codex, visible as a darkening shadow band along the leftmost 40–50 normalized units of the parchment. The stars are drawn on the parchment surface immediately to the right of this shadow, in the narrow left margin column between x~52 and x~115.
